Earthquake families in catalog v6.0 (nearest-neighbour clustering)

Branch analysis/v60-clusters (commit dc8b3640), 2026-11-26. Private working product; not peer reviewed. Same method, parameters and code as the v5.1 clustering (PR #42; v51_clusters_zbz.py, now with --catalog v6.0), run on catalog v6.0 with its converged Route A magnitudes (D-B091).

What changed against v5.1

  • Inputs. Locations: catalog v6.0 (NonLinLoc in model v0.4.1 with SSST station terms and coherence relocation, D-B100) instead of v5.1. Magnitudes: the converged Route A values of D-B091 carried in the v6.0 catalog (130,348 from the v5.1 table, 764 from the v4.1 table) instead of the stored values used for v5.1. Median change of M (converged minus stored) per region box: AX -0.06, EN -0.26, BL -0.70, GO -0.29, MT -0.29, WA +0.01, OR -0.06, PU +0.02, ON +0.01 (Fig. 1).
  • Events used: 168,861 located earthquakes (v5.1: 168,406); 159 rows without a hypocentre (v5.1: 623) and 3,322 flagged as not earthquakes by the v6.0 event_flag (v5.1: 3,313, from the v5.1 magnitude table's is_earthquake). Above Mc (the analysis set): 30,754 events (v5.1: 30,201).
  • Families: 2,101 in v6.0 against 2,097 in v5.1 (975 / 214 / 912 mainshock-aftershock / swarm / multiplet, against 994 / 200 / 903). Background (single events above Mc): 59.6 % against 62.3 %.
  • Completeness and b, v5.1 -> v6.0 (same Mc rule: maximum curvature + 0.2, largest yearly value). Mc: AX 0.65 -> 0.75, EN 2.35 -> 2.05, BL 2.45 -> 1.75, GO 2.55 -> 2.25, MT 1.95 -> 1.65, WA 1.45 -> 1.65, OR 1.85 -> 1.75, PU 1.25 -> 1.25, ON 1.65 -> 1.65. b: AX 0.72 -> 0.71, EN 0.84 -> 0.86, BL 1.27 -> 1.18, GO 1.14 -> 1.18, MT 1.06 -> 1.05, WA 1.08 -> 1.13, OR 0.88 -> 1.11, PU 1.27 -> 1.27, ON 0.81 -> 0.94. Events above Mc: AX 4,410 -> 3,320, EN 554 -> 680, BL 7,230 -> 9,431, GO 1,199 -> 1,005, MT 7,412 -> 7,620, WA 706 -> 428, OR 398 -> 399, PU 3,906 -> 4,058, ON 4,386 -> 3,813.
  • Of the 2,097 v5.1 families, 1,550 are kept in v6.0, 119 grown, 13 split, 59 merged into a larger family, 2 changed and 354 dissolved (less than half of their events in any v6.0 family). Of the 174 v5.1 families with 20 or more events, 144 are kept, 9 grown, 4 split, 12 merged, 0 changed and 5 dissolved. 429 v6.0 families have no v5.1 counterpart.
  • Cause of the 547 v5.1 families that are not kept: the same status already with the converged magnitudes on the v5.1 locations and not with the v6.0 locations alone: 204 (magnitude change); the reverse: 197 (location change); either change alone gives it: 83; only both together: 63. Families dissolved by the magnitude change: 259 (v5.1 locations) and 270 (v6.0 locations); by the location change: 176 (stored M) and 193 (converged M). Split or merged: magnitude change 35 and 34, location change 85 and 75 (matching table below).
  • Large families that changed: v6.0 family F1140 (BL, 2014-03-11, mainshock-aftershock, 1,049 events, grown against v5.1) holds the v5.1 families F1170 (swarm, 480 events, grown); F1165 (swarm, 104 events, grown); F1167 (swarm, 34 events, grown); F1166 (mainshock-aftershock, 33 events, grown); F1178 (swarm, 33 events, grown). v6.0 family F625 (BL, 2013-01-30, mainshock-aftershock, 422 events, grown against v5.1) holds the v5.1 families F597 (mainshock-aftershock, 128 events, grown). v6.0 family F1939 (BL, 2015-06-27, swarm, 218 events, merged against v5.1) holds the v5.1 families F1948 (swarm, 50 events, merged); F1947 (mainshock-aftershock, 48 events, merged); F1949 (swarm, 36 events, merged).
  • Unchanged: method, parameters (df 1.6, distance floor 0.5 km, link cap max(10 km, 3 L(M))), the nine region boxes, the classification rules, the 2-D epicentral distance of the main run.

Caveats

  • Axial depths in v6.0 are about 0.22 km deeper than in v5.1 (median, SSST passes; D-B100, to be fixed in v6.1). The main run uses epicentral (2-D) distance, so families, parents and thresholds do not use depth. Depth enters the 3-D variants d3 and d3q, the family depth columns (depth_good_*) and the swarm-versus-mainshock depth test; read Axial depths there with this offset in mind.
  • The magnitudes were computed with the v5.1 hypocentres (or the v4 hypocentres for the 764 events not in the v5.1 table) and are not recomputed with the v6.0 hypocentres (catalog README).
  • Fault surfaces v1 were fitted on v5.1 locations. The join is by event ID with the faults piece's assignment (on_surface_strict), as for v5.1; it is not redone with the v6.0 locations (numbers in the fault section).
  • Variant mc_best uses Mc_best of the converged regional Mc map table (/wd1/mdenolle_data/magnitude_converged/mc_maps_v41/mc_regional.csv, rows variant all, period all; converged v4.1 magnitudes on v4 locations); there is no Mc map on v6.0 locations. The main run computes its Mc from the v6.0 magnitudes with the v4 rule.
  • Mc is the largest yearly maximum-curvature value. In the year that sets Mc, the two largest 0.1-unit bins differ by 2-19 % (mc_edge_check.csv; WA: 2010, 40 vs 37 events), so a small change of the magnitudes can move Mc by a bin or two. WA shows the effect: its magnitudes changed by +0.01 (median) and its Mc by +0.20 (1.45 -> 1.65), which changes its analysis set from 706 to 428 events.
  • No coherence relocation in the Mendocino region in v6.0 (D-B098): MT epicentres are the SSST locations. The waveform-review sets P1 and P2 are matched by event ID from the v5.1 review.
  • Migration and the sqrt(t) fits use tier A-C epicentres; the family classification does not use them. Treat fault and swarm-migration results as provisional until a cross-correlation double-difference catalog exists.

Files

  • /wd1/mdenolle_data/catalog_v6/v6.0_analysis/clusters/events_zbz_v60.csv.gz: every catalog row (172,342): class, family, role, parent, eta, position; same columns as events_zbz_v51.csv.gz (region_v51 = catalog region label, identical in v5.1 and v6.0)
  • /wd1/mdenolle_data/catalog_v6/v6.0_analysis/clusters/families_zbz_v60.csv: every family: v5.1 columns plus v51_status / v51Mc_status (matching with the v5.1 run and the v5.1-locations converged-M run); v4_status is against v4.1 with converged M

  • variants/: the twelve sensitivity variants, including storedM
